tracked_issues.title: Audit P0: repair opaque qlty check failures blocking renderer PRs
tracked_issues.goal: Do not let opaque external qlty status block the local renderer release gate when GitHub branch protection does not require it.
tracked_issues.rationale: As of 2026-05-21, master branch protection reports required_status_checks=null and the repository tracks no qlty configuration; qlty is therefore an advisory external signal, not a public-alpha release blocker.

qlty check is documented as a non-blocking external signal in docs/reference/renderer-release-gates.md and .github/workflows/README.md
candidate issue validation can resolve #369 through this deferred manifest classification

deferred_requires_gpu_waivers.test_name: [GaussianSplatting][World][SceneTree][RequiresGPU] World submission renders through the resident instanced route without a streaming system
deferred_requires_gpu_waivers.exclude_pattern: *World submission renders through the resident instanced route*
deferred_requires_gpu_waivers.reason: CRASHES: GPU sort sync-contract violation. 'device already submitted, call sync to wait until done', then a fault in GPUSortingPipeline::_capture_instance_count_sync -> RenderingDevice::buffer_get_data -> _flush_and_stall_for_all_frames -> RenderingDeviceDriverVulkan::command_timestamp_write. || TRIAGE 2026-07-19 (#329): TWO independent defects, both confirmed at file:line; the crash reason above is accurate but incomplete. (1) PRODUCT BUG, user-reachable: GPUSortingPipeline::_capture_instance_count_sync (interfaces/gpu_sorting_pipeline.cpp:1002-1023) calls RenderingDevice::buffer_get_data with no guard on submission state, while _sort_instance_pipeline's same-device branch (:2753-2754) issues gs_device_utils::safe_submit WITHOUT a matching sync and _enqueue_instance_count_readback (:1045-1046) then submits again. buffer_get_data stalls via _flush_and_stall_for_all_frames (servers/rendering/rendering_device.cpp:671), and the second submit trips the ERR_FAIL_COND_MSG at rendering_device.cpp:6323 ('device already submitted'). The path is production-only in reach -- sort_gaussians_gpu (:2922) is called from render_sorting_orchestrator.cpp:891 and :1264 with no test-only hook -- and the module runs on a LOCAL rendering device in production (gaussian_splat_manager.cpp:575), which is exactly the device class for which safe_submit actually submits. The sync-bootstrap branch is on by default (interfaces/sync_policy.h:111-119). Production appears protected only by frame timing, not by contract. (2) TEST BUG: this case sets route_policy=GS_ROUTE_STREAMING (:863-864) and drives GaussianSplatWorld3D, which HONOURS route policy (nodes/gaussian_splat_world_3d.cpp:511-514), so should_prefer_resident_backend (renderer/gaussian_splat_renderer.cpp:2798-2831) must return false with reason 'submission_hint_streaming:world_submission' -- yet :915-916 assert 'resident' and 'submission_hint_resident:world_submission'. A sibling case at :498-499 asserts the contract-correct value for the same policy. The expectations read as written against GaussianSplatNode3D, which hard-pins SUBMISSION_RESIDENCY_HINT_RESIDENT (nodes/gaussian_splat_node_3d.cpp:2457 and :2503, deliberate per the comment at :2445-2450). Un-waiving requires BOTH the submit/sync fix (R3 renderer hot path) and corrected route-policy expectations; fixing only the crash leaves this red.
deferred_requires_gpu_waivers.mitigation: Excluded from its GPU batch via BatchSpec.excludes; the other cases in the same batch still execute. tests/ci/test_gpu_harness_deferred_contract.py fails if this waiver is removed while the exclude remains (or vice versa).

deferred_requires_gpu_waivers.test_name: [GaussianSplatting][World][SceneTree][RequiresGPU] Resident rejection preserves resident diagnostics and skips streaming pivot
deferred_requires_gpu_waivers.reason: CRASHES with the same GPU sort sync-contract signature as the resident-instanced-route case above (shared resident submission path). || TRIAGE 2026-07-19 (#329): same two defects as the resident-instanced-route case above -- the unguarded submit/sync imbalance around _capture_instance_count_sync (PRODUCT BUG, user-reachable), plus a route-policy expectation error: it sets GS_ROUTE_STREAMING (:940-941) on a GaussianSplatWorld3D yet asserts instance_backend_policy == 'resident' (:998), which should_prefer_resident_backend cannot produce for a streaming hint (renderer/gaussian_splat_renderer.cpp:2798-2831). Needs both fixes.

deferred_requires_gpu_waivers.test_name: [GaussianSplatting][World][SceneTree][RequiresGPU] Explicit resident quantization rejection falls back to the legacy resident path
deferred_requires_gpu_waivers.reason: CRASHES with VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST: RenderingDeviceDriverVulkan::on_device_lost via print_lost_device_info during command_queue_execute_and_present, surfacing at device finalize. A real GPU fault on the resident quantization-rejection path. || TRIAGE 2026-07-19 (#329): the test itself is INTERNALLY COHERENT -- it sets GS_ROUTE_RESIDENT (:1027-1028), which takes the early return in should_prefer_resident_backend (renderer/gaussian_splat_renderer.cpp:2803-2807) returning true with reason 'requested_resident_policy', exactly what :1090 asserts. Its assertions match the documented contract, so this is NOT a test bug. The remaining blocker is the GPU fault recorded above (VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST during device finalize), which is a real product-side GPU fault, not a harness artifact. Verdict: PRODUCT BUG, deferred -- R3 renderer territory, larger than the waiver-reduction pass.
deferred_requires_gpu_waivers.mitigation: Excluded from its GPU batch via BatchSpec.excludes; the other cases in the same batch still execute. tests/ci/test_gpu_harness_deferred_contract.py fails if this waiver is removed while the exclude remains (or vice versa).

workflow_enforced_rules.rule: stable/candidate release publication must not be Linux-only
workflow_enforced_rules.enforced_by: .github/workflows/release_builds.yml release_candidate_gate job (fails the stable/tag path unless both build_linux and build_windows succeeded)
workflow_enforced_rules.checker_scope: The contract checker verifies the release_candidate_gate job marker is present; it does not parse the job's runtime both-platform logic.

workflow_enforced_rules.rule: stable/candidate release publication must not allow unmatched release files
workflow_enforced_rules.enforced_by: .github/workflows/release_builds.yml publish_release sets fail_on_unmatched_files to true when channel == stable
workflow_enforced_rules.checker_scope: The contract checker does not parse the fail_on_unmatched_files value; this remains YAML-level enforcement.

workflow_enforced_rules.rule: a stable/candidate (v*) tag must not publish without passing check_renderer_release_gates.py --mode candidate
workflow_enforced_rules.enforced_by: .github/workflows/release_builds.yml release_candidate_gate job runs --mode candidate on the stable/tag path and fails closed when the evidence bundle is absent; publish_release requires release_candidate_gate success
workflow_enforced_rules.checker_scope: The contract checker verifies the release_candidate_gate job marker is present; it does not parse the job's runtime candidate invocation.
workflow_enforced_rules.remaining_gap: No CI lane yet produces the public-alpha candidate evidence bundle (GPU-harness report, benchmark-lane report, artifact SHA/commit-parity, issue snapshot). Until that pipeline is wired (issue #360), the gate fails closed on every real v* tag; a maintainer supplies the bundle out-of-band via RELEASE_CANDIDATE_EVIDENCE.

workflow_enforced_rules.rule: candidate evidence must be bound to the commit being published and to the exact bytes being shipped
workflow_enforced_rules.enforced_by: .github/workflows/release_builds.yml release_candidate_gate passes --expected-commit ${{ github.sha }} and --artifact-sha <group>=<sha256> for each archive built in the run, requires the Linux BUILD-INFO commit to equal the published commit, and writes release-attestation.json; publish_release re-hashes its downloaded payload with tests/ci/release_attestation.py verify and refuses to publish on any mismatch
workflow_enforced_rules.checker_scope: check_renderer_release_gates.py implements and unit-tests the --expected-commit / --artifact-sha bindings (tests/ci/test_renderer_release_gates.py::CandidateSupplyChainBindingTests); the attestation round-trip is unit-tested in tests/ci/test_release_attestation.py. The contract checker does not parse the workflow YAML that wires these flags.
workflow_enforced_rules.rationale: --mode candidate alone only proves the evidence bundle is internally consistent, so a stale bundle from an older validated commit could authorize publishing newer, never-validated binaries.

benchmark_acceptance.fallback_route_policy: fail unless lane explicitly allows exact fallback route

unbatched_requires_gpu_backlog.note: [RequiresGPU] test cases that match NO named batch in tests/ci/run_gpu_harness.py and therefore execute nowhere. These are NOT waivers: unlike deferred_requires_gpu_waivers (each proven failing, with an owner and an expiry) these cases have simply never been run, so nothing is known about them. Discovered while landing #329, which addressed only the 28 [SceneTree] cases; measuring the whole corpus with correct doctest semantics showed the gap is larger. Recorded explicitly so it is counted and cannot grow silently: tests/ci/test_gpu_harness_deferred_contract.py fails on any orphan NOT listed here, so this list is a ratchet that may only shrink.
unbatched_requires_gpu_backlog.why_not_covered_by_headless_lanes: Every lane in tests/ci/run_module_tests.py:MODULE_TEST_FILTERS carries the exclude '*][RequiresGPU]*', so zero [RequiresGPU] cases execute headless. The one lane that would match them, 'GaussianSplatting [requires-RD]', is catalogue-only, non-strict, runs solely under --run-gpu, and no workflow passes --run-gpu.
